Cost model is formulaic function of novelty_prop, not 'executed honest sum counters' as claimed. Lines 393-403 compute resolve/bind/verify/browser_steps as deterministic functions of novelty_prop (derived from catalog lookup) plus small hash jitter. rho_novelty=0.8998 is tautological: cost is explicitly designed to track novelty_fraction. The 'honest executed sum counters' claim in prereg measurement_validity[2] and result.json validity_notes[2] is false.

PC-HONEST-COST-SANITY control misimplements 'within-family std>0 for every non-constant stratum' (prereg line 90). Code at lines 741-744 checks pooled std across all families within each novelty stratum (pooled_std=2.73 passes) but 42 of 180 family-novelty cells (23%) have within-family std=0.0 (e.g., family 0,2,5,9,14,16,18,22,23,31,34 at novelty=0.0 all have std=0.0). Validity note 5 admits 'build cost hand-chosen risk mitigated via counted offline vector-ops frozen before outcomes (30 spider, 20 rag ops*0.00002)' but 30 ops is not the actual count.

NC-BIJECTIVE-COST threshold too weak: |rho_proxy_nov|=0.900 vs novelty*3200 proxy (gap=0.899) passes |rho|<1.0 and gap>0.30 but 0.90 indicates near-bijective coupling. The control should require |rho_proxy|<0.50 or gap>0.50 to meaningfully discriminate bijective cost. Current threshold allows cost models that are essentially novelty_fraction scalings to pass.
